Outbreak of Respiratory Illness Hits Turkey’s Transportation & Logistics Industry

A sudden outbreak of a respiratory illness has disrupted operations across Turkey’s Transportation & Logistics industry, with dozens of companies reporting workforce shortages and site closures this week. The illness, identified as a novel strain of viral pneumonia by regional health authorities, was first detected at a major freight terminal in Istanbul late last week and has since spread to several key logistics hubs in the country.

Industry sources say that at least 17 distribution centers and warehousing sites operated by leading firms such as Eksen Lojistik and TransAnadolu have reported clusters of symptomatic workers. Several facilities along the Marmara and Aegean coasts have temporarily ceased operations for deep cleaning and containment measures. According to the Turkish Transportation & Logistics Federation, workforce absenteeism in affected areas is averaging 28% and has exceeded 40% at some large intermodal terminals.

“The situation is evolving rapidly. We are working closely with local health authorities to ensure the safety of our staff and the continuity of our operations,” said Nuray Demirtaş, spokesperson for Yıldız Taşıma, one of Istanbul’s largest logistics operators. “Where possible, we have shifted to split shifts and remote coordination, but extensive disruptions are unavoidable.”

Union representatives have raised concerns about the adequacy of protective measures and sick leave provisions. “Our members are on the front lines and need clear protocols and support,” said İsmail Tuncer, chairperson of the Turkish Logistics Workers’ Union. “We urge all firms to prioritize health and safety above all else.”

Analysts warn that if the outbreak is not contained soon, further operational slowdowns are likely, particularly at cross-docking centers and regional consolidation hubs. “The Transportation & Logistics industry is highly interconnected. Even isolated site closures can create cascading delays,” noted industry consultant Aylin Şahin.

As the situation develops, the Turkish Transportation & Logistics Federation has called for urgent coordination across companies and sites, as well as regular updates to workers. No timeline has yet been set for the full resumption of affected operations.
